summary: Design the engine seams to make /fork (fork_conversation impl) and /recap (new generate_recap primitive) actually work, then wire both into the TUI

research.findings:
CONCRETE fork_conversation IMPL DESIGN. All machinery exists; the only real work is (a) threading a spawner + budget enforcer into the live handle, (b) an override on it, (c) deciding the ForkOutcome.name source.

CORRECTION to the task premise: the live OrchestratorHandle impl is NOT in apps/engine-desktop. It is `impl OrchestratorHandle for ConversationOrchestrator` at orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs:36. That is the ONLY production impl (others are test stubs: platform-api/src/orchestrator_test.rs:246, orchestrator/src/test_support.rs:852, commands/core/src/recap.rs:190). So the fork_conversation override lands there, and the spawner must be threaded INTO ConversationOrchestrator (not into a separate engine-desktop impl).

(1) DEPS THE HANDLE HOLDS (ConversationOrchestrator, conversation.rs:679-975): config, api, streaming_api, tools:Arc<ToolRegistry> (687), hooks, perms, output, session:Arc<Mutex<SessionState>> (691, holds history), memory, cwd, mcp_registry/hook_registry/agent_catalog/compaction (all Option, wired via with_* builders), current_turn_system_prompt:Mutex<Option<String>> (883 — the rendered parent system-prompt bytes recorded by the turn driver, EXACTLY what the fork child needs for a cache-identical prefix). CRITICAL GAP: the orchestrator holds NO SubagentSpawner and NO BudgetEnforcerHandle. Both must be added as new Option fields + with_* builders (same pattern as mcp_registry/compaction at conversation.rs, e.g. with_agent_catalog:1404).

(2) SPAWNER MACHINERY. Trait `SubagentSpawner` (platform-api/src/subagent_spawn.rs:412) — the async entry point is `spawn_async(&self, request:SubagentSpawnRequest, inherit:SubagentInheritance) -> Result<AsyncLaunch,SubagentSpawnError>` (:499). Its DEFAULT returns Internal("not wired") (:504); the ONLY working override is BackgroundAgentSpawner::spawn_async (apps/engine-desktop/src/background_agent.rs:92-149) — spawns a backgrounded LocalAgent via TaskRegistry, registers a mailbox, starts the teammate pump, returns AsyncLaunch{agent_id:protocol::AgentId, output_file:String} (:325). So /fork MUST be handed the BackgroundAgentSpawner (built at apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs:4335 as `Arc<dyn SubagentSpawner>`), NOT the bare PoolSubagentSpawner. SubagentInheritance{tool_invoker:Arc<dyn ToolInvoker>, budget:Arc<dyn BudgetEnforcerHandle>} (:339). Message builders in platform-api/src/fork_subagent.rs: build_child_message(directive)->String (:98, byte-exact boilerplate + "Your directive: {directive}"), build_forked_messages(directive, assistant:&ConversationMessage)->Vec<ConversationMessage> (:161 — clones the parent Assistant, appends one placeholder tool_result per tool_use + the directive text). FORK_SUBAGENT_TYPE="fork" (:36). EXISTING CALLER (the template): tools/agent/src/agent.rs fork path — is_fork branch at :1185, builds fork_context_messages via build_forked_messages(&parsed.prompt, last_assistant) (:1550-1576), builds SubagentSpawnRequest with subagent_type="fork"/model=None/name=None/isolation=None (:841-877, fork_context_messages filled after), builds inherit via RegistryToolInvoker::new(parent_registry) + budget.clone() (:1531-1540), and for run_in_background dispatches spawn_async (:1505). RegistryToolInvoker is at tool-api/src/tool_invoker_impl.rs:19.

(3) fork.rs SEMANTICS (commands/core/src/fork.rs, verified). ForkHandler::handle (:102): trim directive → empty ⇒ "Usage: /fork <directive>"; is_coordinator_session().await true ⇒ "Forking is not available in coordinator sessions. Use /branch instead."; conversation_transcript().await last must be ConversationMessage::Assistant else "Cannot fork before the first conversation turn"; else fork_conversation(directive).await → Ok(ForkOutcome{name,agent_id}) renders "⑂ forked {name} ({tail})" where tail=last 4 chars of agent_id (FORK_ICON=U+2442, :83), Err ⇒ "Could not fork conversation: {msg}". The handler NEVER touches spawning (composition-root concern). ForkOutcome{name:String, agent_id:String} is platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs:94; fork_conversation trait method default = Err(Unimplemented("fork_conversation")) at :789; is_coordinator_session default=false at :778; conversation_transcript default at :766. HandleError::Unimplemented at :118 / ActionFailed at :112.

(4) CONCRETE fork_conversation OVERRIDE (add to orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs, on ConversationOrchestrator):
  a. `let Some(spawner)=self.subagent_spawner.as_ref() else return Err(ActionFailed("fork: no spawner wired"))` (new Option field).
  b. `let history=self.session.lock().await.history.clone();` find last Assistant (rev().find matches!(Assistant)); None ⇒ Err(ActionFailed) — the command already gates this but be defensive.
  c. `let fork_msgs=platform_api::fork_subagent::build_forked_messages(directive, assistant);`
  d. `let parent_sys=self.current_turn_system_prompt.lock().await.clone();` (cache-identical prefix; may be None).
  e. Build SubagentSpawnRequest{ subagent_type:FORK_SUBAGENT_TYPE.into(), prompt:String::new() (fork path seeds empty prompt_messages — directive already lives in the prefix), fork_context_messages:Some(fork_msgs), fork_parent_system_prompt:parent_sys, run_in_background:true, description:Some(short-directive), depth:0, name:None, model:None, isolation:None, ...every OTHER field None/empty } — NOTE SubagentSpawnRequest has NO Default derive (20+ fields, frozen-crate), so every field must be spelled out; mirror agent.rs:841-877.
  f. `let invoker:Arc<dyn ToolInvoker>=Arc::new(RegistryToolInvoker::new(self.tools.clone()));` `let inherit=SubagentInheritance{tool_invoker:invoker, budget:self.budget_enforcer.clone().ok_or(ActionFailed)?};` (budget = new Option field).
  g. `let launch=spawner.spawn_async(request, inherit).await.map_err(|e|ActionFailed(e.to_string()))?;`
  h. `Ok(ForkOutcome{ name:<derived>, agent_id:launch.agent_id.to_string() })`.

DEPS TO THREAD (2 new Option fields + with_* builders on ConversationOrchestrator, wired at apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs): (i) `subagent_spawner:Option<Arc<dyn SubagentSpawner>>` set to the BackgroundAgentSpawner already built at lib.rs:4335; (ii) `budget_enforcer:Option<Arc<dyn BudgetEnforcerHandle>>` set to the one built at lib.rs:3205. self.tools already exists; RegistryToolInvoker is in tool-api (already a dep). This exactly matches the established Option-field + with_* pattern (mcp_registry, compaction, agent_catalog).

risks: ForkOutcome.name has NO source: AsyncLaunch (platform-api/src/subagent_spawn.rs:325) carries only agent_id + output_file, no name. fork_conversation must DERIVE a display name (e.g. a generated codename, or the 'fork' type + id-tail). claude's `t$o` returns a real `o.name`. DECISION NEEDED — no existing agent-name generator was found for the fork path (coordinator::generate_unique_team_name at tool_team_create.rs:215 is team-scoped). Simplest faithful choice: register a generated name via spawner.register_name and echo it.

Layering choice: adding subagent_spawner + budget_enforcer fields to ConversationOrchestrator pulls spawner types into the orchestrator crate. Alternative = a composition-root OrchestratorHandle DECORATOR in engine-desktop that overrides only fork_conversation — but it would have to delegate ~30 other trait methods (heavy). Recommended: the 2-field + with_* approach (matches existing mcp_registry/compaction/agent_catalog Option pattern); flag the layering tradeoff.

is_coordinator_session stays default=false: ConversationOrchestrator has no coordinator-mode state (grep found none in conversation.rs/config). The ForkHandler coordinator gate will therefore never trigger via the live handle unless coordinator mode is also threaded — acceptable for now (coordinator sessions use a different handle path), but note the gate is effectively inert on this handle.

fork_conversation runs the fork DETACHED (spawn_async, run_in_background:true) with output to output_file; the /fork command returns immediately with name+id and does NOT monitor completion — matches claude's local-jsx `t$o` shape, but means no in-TUI surfacing of the fork's result beyond the confirmation line.

current_turn_system_prompt (conversation.rs:883) is None until the first successful turn; fork_parent_system_prompt=None then falls back to the spawner building the child's own system prompt (busting cache identity). Benign but means the very-first-turn fork won't be cache-identical.

budget_enforcer as Option: if left None in any non-desktop composition root (e.g. engine-mobile), fork_conversation must fail with a clear ActionFailed rather than panic on unwrap — spell the None branch explicitly.

research.findings:
DESIGN of the new `generate_recap` primitive. The recap module doc's "same forked-agent-runner machinery /compact's force_compact uses" is NOT the history-mutating `process_iteration`/`force_compact_with_cancel` wrapper — it is the LOWER-level `sidequery::ForkedAgentRunner` + `CacheSafeParamsSlot` that the compactor's Autocompactor invokes internally. Recap reuses those two objects DIRECTLY, skipping every history-swap step, which gives transcript-skip + cache-write-skip + tool-denial for free.

== WHAT force_compact actually does (and why recap must NOT copy it wholesale) ==
`ConversationOrchestrator::force_compact_with_cancel` (orchestrator/src/conversation.rs:1925) snapshots history, runs `compactor.process_iteration(history,0)` (conversation.rs:1979) — which snips/microcompacts/summarizes (compaction/src/orchestrator.rs:185 process_iteration_tracked) — then MUTATES the live session via `apply_post_compact` (conversation.rs:1993: boundary marker + history swap + JSONL persist + CompactionCompleted emit). That mutation is exactly what /recap must never do (recap.rs:20-23 skipTranscript/skipCacheWrite; recap.rs:130-134 "force_compact would truncate history"). So recap does NOT call process_iteration/force_compact at all.

== The primitive to reuse: ForkedAgentRunner::run ==
`ForkedAgentRunner::run` (sidequery/src/forked_agent.rs:202-255) IS the isolated single-turn tool-denied side query: it replays `cache_safe_params.fork_context_messages` (parent history snapshot) FIRST, then appends `req.prompt_messages` (forked_agent.rs:215-216); reuses the parent's rendered `system_prompt` verbatim with `skip_system_prompt_prefix:true` (forked_agent.rs:224,242) for the cache hit; sets `tools: Vec::new(), tool_choice: None` (forked_agent.rs:228-229) → TOOL-DENIED BY CONSTRUCTION; issues exactly ONE `SideQueryClient::query` (maxTurns=1, forked_agent.rs:245); returns `final_text`+usage and NEVER writes session history or the slot. This satisfies all four recap requirements (single-turn, tool-denied, transcript-skipping, cache-write-skipping) with zero new isolation logic.

== The exact request-build template: Autocompactor::compact ==
The autocompactor's forked-summary path (compaction/src/autocompact.rs:182-265) is the byte-level template recap mirrors: `slot.get_last().await` (autocompact.rs:183, returns an owned clone) → build `ForkedAgentRequest { prompt_messages: vec![ConversationMessage::user(MessageId::new(), <prompt>)], cache_safe_params, fork_label, query_source, max_output_tokens }` (autocompact.rs:222-233) → `runner.run(req)` (autocompact.rs:234). Recap differs ONLY in: (a) prompt text = RECAP_PROMPT instead of compact_user_prompt; (b) it STOPS after `runner.run` — no `get_compact_user_summary_message`, no `CompactionResult`, no history write-back; (c) smaller max_output_tokens (recap is <40 words; e.g. 256 vs compaction's 20_000 DEFAULT_FORK_MAX_TOKENS at forked_agent.rs:48).

== The slot that feeds it ==
`cache_safe_slot: Option<Arc<sidequery::CacheSafeParamsSlot>>` is already a field on ConversationOrchestrator (conversation.rs:869), wired via `with_cache_safe_slot` (conversation.rs:1730) and populated after every successful API call by `save_cache_safe_params` (conversation.rs:1763-1791), which stores `fork_context_messages = session.history.clone()` + rendered `system_prompt`. `.get_last()` returns an owned clone. Recap READS this slot but must NEVER call `save_cache_safe_params` again (that is the only slot-writer; not calling it = skipCacheWrite holds automatically).

== WIRING GAP: the orchestrator can't reach a runner ==
ConversationOrchestrator holds the slot but NOT a ForkedAgentRunner — the runner lives buried inside Autocompactor (compaction/src/autocompact.rs:103) inside CompactionOrchestrator (via with_autocompactor), with no accessor. FIX: add a field `recap_runner: Option<Arc<sidequery::ForkedAgentRunner>>` + builder `with_recap_runner` on ConversationOrchestrator, wired at the desktop composition root by CLONING the SAME `forked_runner` Arc already built at apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs:3812-3823 (it is an Arc; the SAME `cache_safe_slot` from lib.rs:3805 is already handed to both the summarizer and the orchestrator). Precedent for a per-purpose runner living on the orchestrator already exists: `SessionMemoryHandle.runner: Arc<ForkedAgentRunner>` (conversation.rs:1104). Mobile (apps/engine-mobile/src/host.rs:1052) wires it identically or leaves recap_runner=None → default Unimplemented.

== RecapOutcome (define in platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs next to ForkOutcome ~:94) ==
enum RecapOutcome { Text(String), Cancelled }. Text carries the trimmed model text (spec item 3) OR — when the forked query itself returned an API-error assistant message — that error's own text (item 4; the runner surfaces it as final_text either way, so no branching needed). Cancelled = spec item 5 → recap.rs maps to fixed "Recap cancelled.". NoTurn (item 1) is NOT in the enum: recap.rs already gates it via conversation_transcript BEFORE calling (recap.rs:122-128). Internal failure (item 6) = `Err(HandleError)` → recap.rs maps to GENERIC_FAILURE_MESSAGE.

== Trait method (platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs, defaulted like fork_conversation ~:789) ==
`async fn generate_recap(&self) -> Result<RecapOutcome, HandleError> { Err(HandleError::Unimplemented("generate_recap".into())) }`. Additive default → mobile/mock/REPL impls unaffected, identical shape to the fork_conversation default.

== Live impl (orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs, on ConversationOrchestrator; force_compact sits at handle_impl.rs:91) ==
`async fn generate_recap(&self){ self.generate_recap_query(CancellationToken::new()).await }` delegating to a NEW inherent `ConversationOrchestrator::generate_recap_query(&self, cancel)` in conversation.rs, modeled on force_compact_with_cancel BUT history-inert:
1. `let runner = self.recap_runner.clone().ok_or(HandleError::ActionFailed("recap unavailable"))?;`
2. `let params = self.cache_safe_slot.as_ref().ok_or(..)?.get_last().await.ok_or(HandleError::ActionFailed("no cache-safe params"))?;` (empty slot = no successful turn yet; unreachable past recap.rs's has_qualifying_turn gate but mapped to Failed defensively).
3. Build ForkedAgentRequest { prompt_messages: vec![user(MessageId::new(), RECAP_PROMPT)], cache_safe_params: params, fork_label:"recap".into(), query_source: QuerySource::Custom("recap".into()) (or add a `Recap` variant to sidequery/src/purposes.rs:11 — COGS tag only), max_output_tokens: Some(256) }.
4. Race with the SAME `tokio::select!{ biased; () = cancel.cancelled() => return Ok(RecapOutcome::Cancelled), r = runner.run(req) => r }` shape as conversation.rs:1972 — note cancel returns Ok(Cancelled) (a specific fixed-string outcome) NOT Err.
5. `Ok(res) => Ok(RecapOutcome::Text(res.final_text.trim().to_string()))`; `Err(ForkError) => Err(HandleError::ActionFailed(e.to_string()))`.
6. CRITICAL: no session.history access, no apply_post_compact, no save_cache_safe_params, no fire_pre/post_compact. Pure read-only side query.

== recap.rs handler change (commands/core/src/recap.rs) ==
Replace the GAP fallback block (recap.rs:130-141) — keep the has_qualifying_turn gate (recap.rs:122-128) — with `match self.handle.generate_recap().await { Ok(RecapOutcome::Text(t)) => Done{display:Some(t)}, Ok(RecapOutcome::Cancelled) => Done{display:Some("Recap cancelled.".into())}, Err(_) => Done{display:Some(GENERIC_FAILURE_MESSAGE.into())} }`. Promote the test-only RECAP_PROMPT (recap.rs:324) to the production const on the impl side (conversation.rs); keep recap.rs's copy as a byte-audit test.

== KNOWN RESIDUAL: cancellation is dead until dispatch threads a token ==
BuiltinCommandHandler::handle (recap.rs:119) takes no cancel token, so generate_recap() always uses a fresh un-cancelled token → RecapOutcome::Cancelled is unreachable via the palette today (recap.rs module doc already flags this). This mirrors force_compact() (handle_impl.rs:91-97) using a fresh token while force_compact_with_cancel exists for the Ctrl-C-carrying caller. Recommend the same split now: trait `generate_recap(&self)` + a future `generate_recap_with_cancel` for when command dispatch threads a token. The Cancelled arm is wired but inert — an honest seam, not fabricated.
facts: ForkedAgentRunner::run (sidequery/src/forked_agent.rs:202-255) is the isolated single-turn side query: replays cache_safe_params.fork_context_messages then appends prompt_messages (:215-216), reuses parent system_prompt verbatim with skip_system_prompt_prefix=true (:224,:242), sets tools:Vec::new()/tool_choice:None (:228-229) = tool-denied, one SideQueryClient::query (:245), returns final_text+usage, writes NO history/slot.

force_compact_with_cancel (orchestrator/src/conversation.rs:1925) runs compactor.process_iteration (:1979) then MUTATES history via apply_post_compact (:1993) — the history-swap recap must avoid; recap reuses the runner directly, not this wrapper.

Autocompactor::compact (compaction/src/autocompact.rs:182-265) is the request-build template: slot.get_last().await (:183) -> ForkedAgentRequest{prompt_messages:vec![user(prompt)],cache_safe_params,fork_label,query_source,max_output_tokens} (:222-233) -> runner.run(req) (:234).

cache_safe_slot: Option<Arc<CacheSafeParamsSlot>> is already a ConversationOrchestrator field (conversation.rs:869), wired via with_cache_safe_slot (:1730), populated by save_cache_safe_params (:1763-1791) storing fork_context_messages=session.history.clone()+system_prompt; get_last() returns an owned clone.

ConversationOrchestrator holds the slot but NOT a ForkedAgentRunner (runner is buried in Autocompactor at autocompact.rs:103, no accessor) -> must add field recap_runner: Option<Arc<sidequery::ForkedAgentRunner>>+with_recap_runner, cloned from the forked_runner Arc built at apps/engine-desktop/src/lib.rs:3812-3823.
Precedent for a per-purpose runner on the orchestrator: SessionMemoryHandle.runner: Arc<ForkedAgentRunner> (conversation.rs:1104).

The live OrchestratorHandle impl is `impl OrchestratorHandle for ConversationOrchestrator` in orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs:36; force_compact there (:91-97) delegates to force_compact_with_cancel with a fresh CancellationToken — the exact pattern generate_recap should follow.

HandleError (platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs:107) has only ActionFailed(String) and Unimplemented(String); ForkOutcome struct is at :94. RecapOutcome (new enum Text/Cancelled) goes alongside; default trait method returns Err(HandleError::Unimplemented) matching fork_conversation.

recap.rs already implements the has_qualifying_turn gate against conversation_transcript (commands/core/src/recap.rs:106-128); only the GAP fallback (:130-141) is replaced by the generate_recap call. Byte-exact RECAP_PROMPT is at recap.rs:324, GENERIC_FAILURE at :69, 'Recap cancelled.' at :336.

tokio::select!{biased; cancel.cancelled() ... ; runner.run(req)} mirrors the cancel-race at conversation.rs:1972-1981, but recap returns Ok(RecapOutcome::Cancelled) on cancel (a fixed-string outcome), not Err.
QuerySource (sidequery/src/purposes.rs:11-37) has Compaction/PostTurnSummary/Custom(String); recap can use Custom("recap") or add a Recap variant — COGS tag only, no behavioral effect.

Cancellation residual: BuiltinCommandHandler::handle (recap.rs:119) has no cancel-token param, so generate_recap()'s fresh token makes RecapOutcome::Cancelled unreachable via palette today — same inert-seam situation as force_compact() vs force_compact_with_cancel.
risks: Empty cache-safe slot: if get_last() returns None (no successful API turn recorded), recap fails to GENERIC_FAILURE. The has_qualifying_turn gate (recap.rs) checks the TRANSCRIPT, but the slot is only populated by save_cache_safe_params after a successful call — a resumed session whose history was loaded from JSONL but has had no live turn yet would pass the transcript gate but have an empty slot. Map to Err(ActionFailed)->GENERIC_FAILURE (acceptable) rather than panic.

recap_runner and cache_safe_slot must be the SAME pair the summarizer uses (both cloned from lib.rs:3805/3812); if a second independent runner/slot is wired, recap replays a stale/empty prefix. Reuse the existing Arcs, do not construct new ones.

RECAP_PROMPT duplication: production const on the impl side (conversation.rs) + byte-audit test copy in recap.rs:324 can drift. Keep the recap.rs test asserting the exact literal so a mismatch fails CI.
max_output_tokens must be set small (recap <40 words); if left at DEFAULT_FORK_MAX_TOKENS (20_000, forked_agent.rs:48) the call still works but over-allocates. Cosmetic, not correctness.
Cancelled arm is wired but inert until command dispatch threads a Ctrl-C token into BuiltinCommandHandler::handle; do not claim /recap is cancellable in user-facing notes.

research.findings:
BLAST RADIUS + TUI UN-DEFER for making /fork and /recap live.

CORRECTION to the task premise: there is exactly ONE live `impl OrchestratorHandle` — `impl OrchestratorHandle for ConversationOrchestrator` at orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs:36. There is NO OrchestratorHandle impl in apps/engine-desktop. Both composition roots use the orchestrator AS the handle: engine-desktop lib.rs:4941 `let handle: Arc<dyn OrchestratorHandle> = orch.clone();` and engine-mobile host.rs:1101 identical. So BOTH overrides (`fork_conversation`, new `generate_recap`) land in orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs, and the fork/recap MACHINERY (which lives in engine-desktop) must be threaded INTO the orchestrator via a new injected `with_...` seam (the same pattern as `with_compaction`/`with_cache_safe_slot`). engine-desktop is still where the seam is CONSTRUCTED and wired, but not where the trait method is implemented.

(1) TRAIT IMPLS THAT MUST COMPILE after adding `generate_recap` + `RecapOutcome`: three impls exist — ConversationOrchestrator (handle_impl.rs:36), MockOrchestratorHandle (orchestrator/src/test_support.rs:647, which overrides ONLY force_compact at :865), and TranscriptStub (commands/core/src/recap.rs:190, a hand-written full impl). A DEFAULTED `generate_recap` (returning e.g. Err(HandleError::Unimplemented) or a NoTurn/Failed variant) keeps all three compiling untouched — confirmed: MockOrchestratorHandle and TranscriptStub both already inherit the existing defaulted `fork_conversation`/`is_coordinator_session` without listing them, so they inherit a new defaulted method the same way. engine-mobile adds no new impl (it reuses ConversationOrchestrator). CONFIRMED: additive default = zero forced edits to mocks.

(2a) fork.rs HANDLER NEEDS NO CHANGES. commands/core/src/fork.rs already calls is_coordinator_session (:114), conversation_transcript (:127), and fork_conversation (:136), and renders ForkOutcome→"⑂ forked {name} ({tail})". ForkOutcome (platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs:94), the `fork_conversation` trait method + its Unimplemented default (:789), and HandleError::Unimplemented (:118) all already exist. The ONLY work is the live override.

(2b) recap.rs HANDLER NEEDS A CHANGE. Today after the no-turn gate (recap.rs:123 via has_qualifying_turn) it UNCONDITIONALLY emits GENERIC_FAILURE (:135-141). To wire: after the gate passes, call the NEW `self.handle.generate_recap().await` seam and map outcomes → success text / "Recap cancelled." / GENERIC_FAILURE. `generate_recap` + `RecapOutcome` do NOT exist yet and must be added to platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs next to ForkOutcome/fork_conversation. The byte-exact RECAP_PROMPT (currently a test-only const at recap.rs:324) and CANCELLED_MESSAGE (:336) move into the SEAM impl (the orchestrator owns the forked query), since the handler only renders the returned text.

THE REAL BLAST RADIUS (engine seams — the hard part, NOT in commands/core):

risks: PREMISE CORRECTION (must-heed): the override does NOT go in apps/engine-desktop — the only OrchestratorHandle impl is on ConversationOrchestrator (orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs:36). Implementing in engine-desktop is impossible; the machinery must be threaded INTO the orchestrator via with_* seams. Building against a nonexistent engine-desktop impl is the single biggest way to waste the effort.

ForkOutcome.name has NO source in AsyncLaunch (agent_id + output_file only, verified subagent_spawn.rs:326-331). fork_conversation MUST synthesize a name and set both request.name and ForkOutcome.name (optionally spawner.register_name). Forgetting this yields an empty '⑂ forked  (tail)'. OPEN DECISION: name scheme (codename vs 'fork-{4hex}' vs directive slug) — any stable non-empty string satisfies the render.

recap MUST reuse ForkedAgentRunner::run directly, NOT force_compact/self.compaction — force_compact_with_cancel (conversation.rs:1925) mutates history via apply_post_compact. Wiring recap to force_compact by analogy would DESTROY conversation history (spec: read-only, skipTranscript/skipCacheWrite).

forked_runner is MOVED into Autocompactor at lib.rs:3825; recap_runner must be CLONED from the same Arc BEFORE that move (and cache_safe_slot is already shared). A second independently-constructed runner/slot would replay a stale/empty prefix. Reuse the existing Arcs.

SubagentSpawnRequest has NO Default derive (~20 fields) — every field must be spelled out mirroring agent.rs:841-877; on the fork path prompt=String::new() (directive lives inside fork_context_messages) and run_in_background=true. Easy to get a field wrong; copy the agent.rs literal.

/fork MUST be ArgSpec::Optional not Required — Required makes bare '/fork' fall through as an LLM prompt, hiding the handler's 'Usage: /fork <directive>' (fork.rs:105) — a silent regression vs claude-code.

Empty cache-safe slot: a resumed session (history loaded from JSONL, no live turn yet) passes recap's transcript gate but get_last() returns None → map to Err(ActionFailed)→GENERIC_FAILURE (acceptable), never panic on unwrap. Same defensive-None for fork_budget/fork_spawner on non-desktop roots.

Cancelled arm is WIRED BUT INERT until command dispatch threads a Ctrl-C token into BuiltinCommandHandler::handle (recap.rs:119 takes none) — do NOT claim /recap is cancellable in user-facing notes (mirrors force_compact()'s fresh-token limitation).
is_coordinator_session stays default=false on this handle (no coordinator state on ConversationOrchestrator) → the /fork coordinator gate is effectively inert here; acceptable but note it.

Adding RecapOutcome/generate_recap edits the shared platform-api/src/orchestrator.rs and adds struct fields the fork.rs/recap.rs module docs flagged as out-of-scope for the handler task — this is the integration pass; run the full-workspace check to catch broken mock/literal sites (engine-mobile, test_support, recap.rs TranscriptStub all inherit the new defaulted method automatically, but verify).
open_questions: ForkOutcome.name generation scheme — no fork-path name generator exists (coordinator::generate_unique_team_name is team-scoped). Pick: short codename, 'fork-{4hex}', or directive-slug. Render only shows name + id-tail so any stable non-empty string works.
QuerySource for recap: reuse QuerySource::Custom("recap") (purposes.rs:11-37) or add a dedicated Recap variant — COGS/telemetry tag only, no behavioral effect. Custom is zero-risk.
recap max_output_tokens: recommend Some(256) (recap is <40 words) vs compaction's DEFAULT_FORK_MAX_TOKENS 20_000 — cosmetic over-allocation only if left large.

Whether to add the two optional MockOrchestratorHandle overrides (shared test_support.rs) for success-render tests, or keep test_support untouched and use local tui-test stubs (precedent: recap.rs TranscriptStub). Local stubs keep the shared file clean.

Fork approach: recommended 2 raw Option fields (orchestrator already deps tool-api+cost, holds tools registry) vs a narrow ForkSpawner seam trait constructed at the composition root (cleaner layering, more boilerplate). Confirm the raw-field approach is acceptable given it pulls RegistryToolInvoker/SubagentInheritance into orchestrator/src/handle_impl.rs.
